summary:
BEYOND is an interactive, browser-based 3D space exploration game designed to turn passive curiosity about the universe into active hands-on discovery. Built around a first-person spacecraft cockpit with a live telemetry HUD, players pilot across multi-chapter missions—from breaking Earth's orbit to crossing the 384,400 km lunar distance and venturing toward Mars—unlocking verified planetary science along the way.

Space science often feels distant and abstract when consumed solely through textbooks or videos. BEYOND bridges this gap by combining gameplay with real aerospace education: players aren't just playing, they are learning orbital mechanics, thrust management, and mission planning using real data sourced via a live NASA API key (including NASA APOD and JPL planetary metrics).

By making space exploration tangible and interactive, BEYOND empowers students, educators, and future innovators to experience how real missions work.
details:
It is an interactive, browser-based 3D space exploration simulation that puts players directly inside the pilot’s seat of a spacecraft. Across a structured four-chapter story charter—Leaving Earth (384,400 km lunar crossing), The Red Frontier (225 million km trans-Mars burn), Outer Worlds, and Recovered Data—players manage thrust, heading alignment, cruise velocity, fuel burn, and arrival logic through a real-time cockpit flight HUD. Each completed flight unlocks recovered data logs, turning mission progression into active science discovery.

Benefits & Intended Impact Traditional space education often relies on passive reading or videos, leaving orbital mechanics and planetary scale feeling abstract. BEYOND transforms learners from passive spectators into active pilots—you are not just playing, you are learning how real spacecraft navigate. Our intended impact is to give students, educators, and space enthusiasts an accessible, hands-on simulation that connects classroom physics with authentic aerospace missions, inspiring the next generation of explorers and innovators.

Tools, Technologies & Data Sources

  • Platform & Web Stack: Built with Base44, modern web technologies (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and WebGL/3D rendering) for instant, zero-install browser play.
  • NASA Open Data & API Integration: Integrated a live NASA API key to pull Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) data alongside verified planetary metrics from the NASA/JPL Earth’s Moon Fact Sheet (384,400 km mean distance, 27.32-day orbit, 1,737.4 km radius) and mission context from NASA’s Artemis II Press Kit.

Creativity & Key Considerations Rather than building a static space encyclopedia or an arcade shooter with exaggerated physics, we combined immersive first-person cockpit telemetry with a narrative data-recovery loop. A core factor our team considered was scientific integrity: ensuring real propulsion concepts, planetary distances, and NASA-verified facts are clearly distinguished from speculative deep-space technologies, while keeping browser performance smooth and intuitive for learners of all backgrounds.
